answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through an invite-graph debt mechanism where each new identity is tied to a verified sponsor. The initial cost for the inviter starts at 10 tokens, increasing by 5 tokens for each additional identity they create. By the time they reach 10 identities, the financial burden escalates to 60 tokens. This structure acts like a willow tree; as too many branches emerge, the trunk becomes unable to support the weight, ensuring that an attacker cannot thrive without substantial investment, much like an onyx prism reflecting the costs of their actions.
